sonnet.q1: The scheduler starts attempt 1 at 02:00 UTC. Extract reads every orders row (all columns) from the replica with updated_at later than the watermark minus 2 hours, with no upper bound.
sonnet.q2: A bulk import is an app transaction that can stay open up to 90 minutes. Its rows get updated_at when written, so they become visible up to 90 minutes after their updated_at.
sonnet.q3: The edit sets updated_at to the write time. The next nightly extract reads it (updated_at after watermark minus 2h) and the merge replaces the fact_orders row if the staged updated_at is later.
sonnet.q4: The app never hard-deletes; it sets deleted_at (a write that sets updated_at). The next extract picks it up and the merge replaces the row including deleted_at and sets is_deleted true. The row stays in fact_orders.
sonnet.q5: The attempt rolls back (no change to fact_orders, watermark or success row) and writes a failure row to etl_runs with run date, attempt number and error. If the highest attempt number is below 3, the next attempt starts 15 minutes after the failure row. After the third failure, on-call is paged and the night's run stops with the watermark unchanged.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards show the last committed night. The 06:00 check finds no success row for the run date and posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts (on-call is paged only if the third attempt failed).
sonnet.q7: The next Sunday reconciliation. It compares count and checksum per creation date over the last 30 days. The mismatch is found and that day is reloaded from the replica and merged.
sonnet.q8: The merge is keyed on order_id. It updates a row only if the staged updated_at is later than the existing one. If equal or earlier, it leaves the existing row alone.
sonnet.q9: In the warehouse table etl_watermark. It is set to the candidate watermark (the UTC time when the attempt's Extract started). It is written in the same transaction as the merge, at commit.
sonnet.q10: The merge, watermark update and success row are in one warehouse transaction. Commit makes all writes visible at once and a failure rolls back everything. Dashboards read only fact_orders, never stg_orders.
sonnet.q11: The retry's Extract empties stg_orders at the start, so the failed attempt's staged rows are discarded. The retry reads the same unchanged watermark and extracts every order updated after watermark minus 2 hours, with no upper bound.
sonnet.q12: It re-reads all of that day's (creation date) orders from the replica, stages them in stg_orders, and merges them using the step 3 rules in one transaction. It only inserts or replaces, never deletes. It does not move the watermark.
